headline: Warm, dry weather through Friday with possible morning fog, then cooler, lightly showery weather from Saturday into early next week.
summary: High pressure keeps western Washington dry and warm through Friday. Highs should reach the upper 60s to low 70s Thursday and the mid 70s Friday, with some Minor HeatRisk, meaning a small number of heat-sensitive people could be affected. Thursday morning may bring low cloud and possibly fog, but forecasters describe fog only as a possibility. Winds from the east could gust 25-30 mph in the Cascades and foothills Thursday night. Humidity in the Cascades and southern Olympics may drop to around 35-40% Thursday and 35-45% Friday. The weather turns over the weekend as the high weakens and a series of weak systems move through. Saturday will likely bring rain during the day, mostly in the North Cascades. Lowlands should see only a few hundredths of an inch, and parts of the Seattle area may stay dry. Highs drop to the low 60s Saturday. Sunday looks cooler and drier, with morning lows in the low 40s around Puget Sound and the mid 30s in the Cascade foothills. Cool, unsettled weather continues into early next week, with more chances for light rain, especially Tuesday. Seas on the coastal waters build over the weekend and may go higher early next week. Forecasters are fairly confident through Saturday. They say the pattern after Tuesday is unclear because the forecast models disagree, and they will watch the track of an offshore trough on Sunday for changes.
changes: The evening discussion drops the earlier mention of a convergence zone and showers Saturday afternoon, and now expects light, mostly mountain rain on Saturday with some lowlands dry. It also adds details on Minor HeatRisk, possible fog, and low humidity, and describes Sunday as drier instead of showery.
